title: Ecthyma gangrenosum in febrile neutropenia: Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia
vignette: A 55-year-old woman comes to the emergency department with fever and chills. She has a history of acute myeloid leukemia for which she is receiving chemotherapy. Her temperature is 38.3 C (101 F), blood pressure is 90/50 mm Hg, pulse is 124/min, and respirations are 22/min. Physical examination is notable for multiple skin patches with necrotic centers and occasional ulcerations, which appear as necrotic ulcers with a black eschar and surrounding erythema. Laboratory results show platelets 240,000/mm3, leukocytes 800/mm3, neutrophils 60%, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, prothrombin time 12 seconds, and activated partial thromboplastin time 33 seconds. Blood cultures are drawn. Which of the following organisms is most likely responsible for this patient's symptoms?

clues.text: acute myeloid leukemia for which she is receiving chemotherapy
clues.note: Chemotherapy-induced neutropenia in leukemia markedly increases susceptibility to serious bacterial infection (febrile neutropenia).

clues.text: necrotic ulcers with a black eschar and surrounding erythema
clues.note: Skin lesions with necrotic centers/ulceration and surrounding erythema (black eschar) are ECTHYMA GANGRENOSUM, strongly associated with Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia.
Severe leukopenia (leukocytes 800; ANC ~480) = febrile NEUTROPENIA - the setting for Pseudomonas sepsis and ecthyma gangrenosum.

whatMatters: ECTHYMA GANGRENOSUM (necrotic skin ulcers with a black eschar/erythematous halo) in a FEBRILE NEUTROPENIC patient (leukocytes 800) is strongly associated with PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA bacteremia (perivascular invasion + tissue-destructive exotoxins). Normal platelets/coagulation argue against DIC. Answer D.
strategy: Combine host (neutropenia) + lesion (ecthyma gangrenosum) -> Pseudomonas aeruginosa. EG arises from perivascular bacterial invasion and exotoxin-mediated vascular destruction/ischemia. Reject other gram-negatives/streptococci: E coli (gram-negative sepsis, but EG classically Pseudomonas; HUS causes renal failure/thrombocytopenia - absent), Klebsiella (necrotizing pneumonia), H influenzae and S pneumoniae (respiratory), and S pyogenes (cellulitis/erysipelas/necrotizing fasciitis - single site, not multiple EG patches).

eliminations.label: E coli - not classically ecthyma gangrenosum
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the most common cause of gram-negative sepsis (often urinary source). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: E coli is not classically associated with ecthyma gangrenosum; its Shiga-toxin form causes HUS (renal failure/thrombocytopenia), absent here. ✅ Correct if: urosepsis or HUS.

eliminations.label: H influenzae - respiratory
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a respiratory pathogen (pneumonia, epiglottitis, meningitis). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it isn't associated with ecthyma gangrenosum. ✅ Correct if: respiratory/CNS infection.

eliminations.label: Klebsiella pneumoniae - necrotizing pneumonia
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a gram-negative rod causing necrotizing pneumonia (currant-jelly sputum) in the debilitated. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it doesn't classically cause ecthyma gangrenosum skin lesions. ✅ Correct if: necrotizing pneumonia/abscess.

eliminations.label: S pneumoniae - respiratory/meningitis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: encapsulated gram-positive diplococcus (pneumonia, meningitis, sepsis). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: not associated with ecthyma gangrenosum. ✅ Correct if: lobar pneumonia/meningitis.

eliminations.label: S pyogenes - single-site skin infection/fasciitis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: Group A strep causing impetigo, erysipelas, and necrotizing fasciitis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: necrotizing fasciitis is usually a SINGLE rapidly spreading site with pain out of proportion, not multiple ecthyma gangrenosum patches from Pseudomonas bacteremia. ✅ Correct if: single-site necrotizing soft-tissue infection.

reasoning: Febrile neutropenia (leukocytes 800) from chemotherapy predisposes to Pseudomonas sepsis
Skin lesions with necrotic centers, black eschar, and erythematous halo are ecthyma gangrenosum
Ecthyma gangrenosum is strongly associated with Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia
mechanism: ECTHYMA GANGRENOSUM (EG) is a cutaneous NECROTIC lesion classically caused by PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA BACTEREMIA, most often in NEUTROPENIC or otherwise immunocompromised hosts (here chemotherapy for AML with leukocytes 800/ANC ~480). Circulating P aeruginosa invades the walls of dermal/subcutaneous ARTERIES and VEINS (PERIVASCULAR invasion) and releases tissue-destructive EXOTOXINS (exotoxin A - protein synthesis inhibition; elastase - degrades elastin/vessel wall; phospholipase C; pyocyanin - reactive oxygen species). Vascular destruction causes ISCHEMIA and NECROSIS of the overlying skin, producing painless red macules that evolve into hemorrhagic bullae and then punched-out ULCERS with a BLACK ESCHAR and an erythematous halo. Normal platelet count and PT/aPTT here argue against DIC. Pseudomonas infections are common in patients who are neutropenic, hospitalized, burned, or have indwelling catheters. The distractors are not classically linked to EG: E coli (gram-negative/urosepsis, HUS), Klebsiella (necrotizing pneumonia), H influenzae and S pneumoniae (respiratory), and S pyogenes (single-site cellulitis/necrotizing fasciitis).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro > Pseudomonas aeruginosa: ecthyma gangrenosum (necrotic skin ulcer with black eschar) in neutropenia; perivascular invasion + exotoxins (exotoxin A, elastase, phospholipase C, pyocyanin); also burns, catheters, hot-tub folliculitis, otitis externa.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Ecthyma gangrenosum + febrile neutropenia = Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on ecthyma gangrenosum, febrile neutropenia, Pseudomonas exotoxins, or eschar? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: E coli = urosepsis/HUS; Klebsiella = necrotizing pneumonia; H flu/pneumococcus = respiratory; S pyogenes = single-site fasciitis.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: Skin lesion (stem image): necrotic ulcer with a BLACK ESCHAR and erythematous halo = ecthyma gangrenosum -> Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: ecthyma gangrenosum in neutropenia = Pseudomonas aeruginosa (perivascular invasion + exotoxins).
